title: Dynamic programming
summary: Solve each small problem once and reuse it.

cards.title: Remember instead of recompute
cards.body:
Many problems are made of smaller copies of themselves. **Dynamic programming** solves each small copy once, stores the answer in a table, and builds bigger answers from it.

Two questions find a DP solution: what does one table cell mean, and how is it built from smaller cells?

cards.title: Coin change
cards.body: dp[x] = fewest coins for amount x. Notice the final caption: grabbing the biggest coin first (greedy) gives the wrong answer here.

cards.title: Longest common subsequence (2D)
cards.body: Each cell looks at three neighbours: diagonal if the letters match, otherwise up and left.
